checks_run.note: 11 core unit tests and 5 CLI tests, all passing.
`score-jev` is listed. The `--json` run on an empty store is covered by the CLI test `an_empty_store_reports_too_few_labeled_cases_and_exits_cleanly`; I did not run it by hand.

open_issues: Nothing writes `athena.class-label/1` records. Until a label writer exists, the real-records run needs labels created by hand or by a later command (explicitly out of scope).
Item 2 checks only whether the reviewed groups land cleanly. It does not look up R1–R4 or the §3.6 cases, which need real record ids (the design's gate).
`MIN_TEST_CASES = 10`, the 10% false-match limit and the overlap threshold grid are estimates or design choices to be set at review, not measured values.
The interval is a normal approximation and is given only when n > (1.96·sd/mean)², so it only ever appears with a lower bound above zero. That follows §10.4 item 1 as written.
The reply key `answers` in the Jev client is still unverified live; scoring depends on records produced by that client.

The brief listed `jev.rs`, `wiring.rs`, `introspect.rs` and `store.rs` as possible edits. Only `introspect.rs` (one visibility change) and `store.rs` were needed; `jev.rs` and `wiring.rs` are unchanged.
mistakes: My first draft of the main test expected verdict item 2 to be 'not met'. In that fixture every reviewed group maps consistently to one Jev class, so it is correctly 'met'. I fixed the test.
A first draft of the interval test used constant per-record improvements, giving zero spread and a degenerate interval. I varied Jev's confidence in the fixture instead.
The mistyped `format!` with no arguments in `display.rs` was fixed before the first clippy run.
learnings: Introspection records keep Jev's answers in `jev` (`IntrospectionJev`), but `introspect::read_records` drops them, so the new module has its own small reader built on the now `pub(crate)` `month_files`.
Adding an `AnyRecord` variant needs the arm in `store.rs` `Records::load`: its catch-all calls `job_of(...).expect(...)` and would panic on a record with no job.
The CLI opens the repository from the working tree, and `propose` reads `records/` there too, so `score-jev` does the same through `self.git.dir()`. Uncommitted records are therefore read.
Fixture helpers: `common::Fixture` gives a temp git repo plus `ATHENA_STATE_DIR`; binary tests set `current_dir` and that variable. `RecordId::from_parts(ts, n)` makes deterministic ids.
The tool policy blocks reading files outside the working directory, so persisted tool output could not be grepped; use `cargo test -q` for compact output.
Class registry ids are `RecordId`s, and Jev's option set is those ids plus `new`. I treat a reviewer's 'none' as Jev's `new`.
desires: A way to read the output of a long test run, such as grepping persisted tool output inside the working directory.
A sample of real labeled records, to check the 10-case minimum and the reference choice against actual data.
